info.title: API.SH: Glassdoor
info.description: The Glassdoor API from API.SH: public Glassdoor data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.description:
A company's benefits on Glassdoor for one country: the overall benefits rating and number of benefit reviews, every benefit employees reported grouped by category (health insurance, 401K, parental leave, free lunch...) with its rating, number of ratings and reviews and whether the employer verified it, the most talked about benefits with a quote, and a page of benefit reviews (rating, date, text, job title, location, current or former employee, helpful votes; 10 a page). Pass `next_page` back as `page`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/glassdoor-benefits

parameters.name: company
parameters.description: Company name, e.g. `Google`.

parameters.name: employer_id
parameters.description: Glassdoor employer id (e.g. 9079), instead of `company`.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Any glassdoor.com employer link (Overview, Reviews...), instead of `company`.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Country the benefits apply to: a name (`United Kingdom`), a code (`uk`, `de`, `in`) or a Glassdoor country id. Default United States.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page of benefit reviews. Pass `next_page` from the previous response.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Interview reviews for a company on Glassdoor, by name, employer id or link, with paging, sort (newest, relevance, hardest) and filters for experience (positive, neutral, negative), outcome (accepted, declined, no offer) and job title. Each interview: id, job title, interview date and posted date, experience, difficulty, offer outcome, how the candidate applied, duration in days, location, process description, the interview questions, helpful votes and employer responses. Also the filtered and total interview counts, average difficulty, experience and source counts. Pass `next_page` back as `page`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/glassdoor-interviews

get.description:
One Glassdoor job listing by its id (the `id` from Glassdoor jobs) or link: title, full description (text and HTML), apply link and easy apply, posting age and date, expired flag, location with city, state, country and coordinates, job type, remote, pay range with its currency, period and source (employer provided or estimated), skills, education and years of experience, and the employer (rating and category ratings, website, headquarters, size, founding year, type, revenue, industry, CEO) with its most talked about benefits, recent benefit reviews and review highlights. Also `benefits` (the listing''s own benefits), `job_attributes` (every label list the site extracted from the ad) and `salary_estimate_source` (employer_provided or estimated). 404 when the listing has expired or been removed.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/glassdoor-job

parameters.name: url

get.description:
Jobs on Glassdoor for keywords and a location (any country: `country` or a city abroad), with the site's filters (posted within N days, remote, easy apply, salary range, job type). Each job: id, title, company and its rating and logo, location, age in days, easy apply and sponsored flags, pay range (10th/50th/90th percentile, currency, period, source), occupation, description snippet, extracted attributes (skills, benefits, level) and the job link. `total` is Glassdoor's count; 30 per page; `companies` lists the hiring companies in the results. Pass `next_page` back as `page`; null on the last page. Also filters by minimum employer rating, company size and seniority, `radius` in miles around the location, and by industry, hiring company, city, occupation category or the site's job-type code (ids from `filter_options`, which lists each of these menus for the search with its job counts). `sponsored_employer` marks promoted employers. The site has no benefits or sponsored-only filter.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/glassdoor-jobs

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Keywords, e.g. `data analyst`. Required unless `url` is given.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: City, state or country, e.g. `New York`, `Texas`, `United States`.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: A glassdoor.com job search link (/Job/...htm), instead of `q` and `location`.

parameters.name: job_type
parameters.description: fulltime, parttime, contract, internship, temporary.

parameters.name: min_rating
parameters.description: Employer rating at least this many stars.

parameters.name: company_size

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Jobs in this country (us, gb, ca, de, au, in, ie, fr, nl, be, at, ch, es, it, nz, sg, hk, mx, br): narrows `location` to it, or alone searches the whole country. Pay comes in the local currency; the country sites list the same jobs.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: Miles around the location (0, 5, 10, 15, 25, 50 or 100; the site's default is 25).

parameters.name: industry_id

parameters.name: city_id

parameters.name: job_type_code
parameters.description: The site's job type code from `filter_options.job_type_code` (e.g. full-time, contract, per diem).

get.description:
Employee reviews of a company on Glassdoor, with paging, sort (relevance, newest, lowest rating), a text search and a current-employees filter. Each review: id, title, date, overall rating, pros, cons, advice to management, job title, location, current/former, employment status and length, recommend / CEO approval / business outlook, sub-ratings, helpful votes and employer responses. Also the company's ratings, rating distribution and review counts. Pass `next_page` back as `page`; null on the last page. Optional filters: overall star `rating`, reviewer `employment_status`, `job_title` and review `language`; `applied_filters` echoes them.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/glassdoor-reviews

get.description:
Pay on Glassdoor. With `company` (or `employer_id` / `url`): one employer's pay for each of its job titles (total, base and additional pay at the 10th to 90th percentiles, currency, pay period; 5 a page as on the site, sortable), optionally only one `job_title` and one place, plus the employer's rating and open jobs. Otherwise, pay for a job title, nationwide or in a city, metro, state or country: the estimate (total, base and additional pay at the 10th to 90th percentiles, currency, pay period, number of salaries, confidence, last update), what each company pays for that title (employer id, name, logo, rating, open jobs, total-pay percentiles; 5 companies a page as on the site, sortable) and, on page 1, the 10 most recent individual salary reports (pay range, experience, city, date). Filters: years of experience and industry. Pass `next_page` back as `page`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/glassdoor-salaries

parameters.name: job_title
parameters.description: Job title, e.g. `Data Analyst`, `Software Engineer`, `Registered Nurse`. Optional with `company`.

parameters.name: company
parameters.description: Company name, e.g. `Google`: that employer's salaries for each job title.

parameters.name: employer_id
parameters.description: Glassdoor employer id (e.g. 9079), instead of `company`.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Any glassdoor.com employer link, instead of `company`.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: City, state or country, e.g. `New York, NY`, `Texas`, `London`, `United Kingdom`. Leave out for the whole of the United States.

parameters.name: experience
parameters.description: Years of experience for the estimate (default all).

parameters.name: industry_id
parameters.description: Glassdoor industry id for the estimate, e.g. 10013 (Information Technology).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order of the companies (default popular).

parameters.name: recent
parameters.description: 0 leaves out the recent salary reports (default 1).

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page of companies. Pass `next_page` from the previous response.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Company lookup on Glassdoor by name, as the site's own search box suggests it: employer id, name, logo, overall rating and review count (for the first five matches), best-match flag and Overview link. The employer id works in the company, reviews, interviews and salaries endpoints.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/glassdoor-search

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Company name, e.g. `Nike`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Suggestions to return (1-10, default 8).

parameters.name: ratings
parameters.description: 0 = skip the rating lookup (faster).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
